paragraphs: Decision center: The work of door-to-door sales workers and news and street vendors and related workers is to turn front-end conditions such as target customers or foot traffic locations, the goods and samples and explanatory materials carried along, the prices and terms that can be checked on the spot, and the constraints of consumer protection and cash and personal safety into a sales chain that can be completed, reconciled and kept within boundaries — first determine potential customers or a vending location and prepare samples and explanatory materials and payment money and change, then check needs and demonstrate and explain prices and terms, then persuade the purchase and record the order on the spot or deliver and collect payment, then distribute samples and materials and restock and tidy the stall, and finally keep records and follow up on satisfaction and train newcomers when necessary. The focus of judgment is not whether you can sell the goods, but whether every step of the find-people—demonstrate—quote—close—deliver-and-collect—document—follow-up chain states things truthfully, sells at the marked price, keeps vouchers and holds the boundaries of consumer protection and cash and personal safety.

Good to try first: Willing to approach strangers proactively and explain the product clearly face to face; able to stay polite and restrained when rejected or questioned without exaggerating or deceiving; willing to work according to clearly marked prices and voucher and return and cancellation rights requirements; able to stand and walk for long periods, carry goods and accept irregular working hours and performance-based or volume-based pay.

Proceed with caution: If you dislike being rejected or questioned, or are not good at face-to-face communication, or are willing to exaggerate effects and conceal terms and withhold vouchers in order to close a sale (or are unwilling to work according to clearly marked prices and cancellation and refund requirements), or you understand this work as sitting in an office doing online marketing, then the actual work experience usually does not match the expectation.

Low-risk verification: Using the fictional product and price sheet and customer objection list provided on this page, complete a paper exercise of writing a statement of no more than 60 seconds for each of 6 fictional customers, handling 3 common objections, and filling in one order and payment and voucher and return statement. This only verifies whether you are willing to explain face to face, quote truthfully and record truthfully. The exercise uses fictional materials, does not touch real customers or real transactions, makes no price commitments or legal opinions, and is not equivalent to position training or an operating license.

Decision center: Whether target customers and foot traffic locations and the goods carried along and price terms can be organized into a sales and payment record that customers and colleagues can understand and can be checked afterwards.

The workplace is communities and blocks and stalls and temporary sales sites, and the rhythm is determined by foot traffic and weather and season and performance targets.

Similar names do not mean the same duties: This page is O*NET-SOC 41-9091.00 Door-to-Door Sales Workers, News and Street Vendors, and Related Workers. Adjacent positions have different duties — retail salespersons serve in-store customers; first-line supervisors of retail sales workers manage store staff and scheduling and performance; driver/sales workers combine delivery and sales on fixed routes and are responsible for vehicles and goods; advertising sales agents and sales engineers sell media or technical solutions to organizations; sales representatives of services sell services to organizations; cashiers mainly handle cashiering and checkout; demonstrators and product promoters focus on on-site demonstration and promotion; telemarketers focus on telephone communication. The focus of this occupation is direct face-to-face selling: finding people and demonstrating and quoting and closing and delivering and collecting payment and documenting and following up. Consumer protection and business registration and food safety (where food is involved) and tax and the employment form (employee or commission or self-employed) are governed by the laws of the relevant jurisdiction and local rules, are not inferred from the job title, and no one may promise prices externally or give legal or tax conclusions beyond their authorization.

Inputs that must be checked: the true information about the goods or services and the clearly marked price and pricing unit, the deliverability and delivery time and freight and warranty and return and exchange conditions, the cancellation right and cooling-off period and return instructions where applicable, the payment and change and voucher and invoice arrangements, the location and time period of the stall or business site and local registration and urban management requirements, and the safety arrangements for cash and goods and personal information carried. What must not be done: do not exaggerate or falsely describe product effects and prices, do not conceal the total price and additional charges or delivery and return and exchange conditions, do not withhold vouchers or refuse to handle cancellation and refund requirements, do not operate in prohibited areas or during prohibited time periods, do not carry excessive cash or stay alone in an isolated location for long periods without safety arrangements, and do not use customer lists and contact details and payment information for purposes other than work.

The fit judgment should be made by considering whether you can proactively communicate with strangers and explain truthfully, whether you can stay polite and restrained when rejected, whether you can work according to clearly marked prices and voucher and cancellation and refund requirements, whether you can stand and walk for long periods and carry goods and accept irregular hours and performance-based pay, and whether you are clear about your duties and authorization and business compliance boundaries; it should not be replaced by a self-assessment of having good communication skills or knowing many people; all of these must be confirmed in supervised actual positions or real business scenarios.

All exercises on this page use fictional materials; real product sales, quoting, payment collection and vouchers, return and exchange and cancellation right handling, stall operation and business registration, and cash and personal and information security must be undertaken by personnel who meet the corresponding business and employment conditions and act in accordance with the laws of the jurisdiction and local rules; whether the FTC cooling-off rule and Chinese mainland consumer rights protection obligations apply must be checked item by item against amount and location and goods or services and exceptions. Individuals may not promise prices or closing terms externally or give legal, tax or safety conclusions beyond their authorization, and this page does not constitute legal, tax, consumer rights or safety advice.

The work object of this occupation is the face-to-face sales site: target customers and foot traffic locations, the goods and samples and explanatory materials and payment money and change carried along, the customer's real needs and objections and budget, quotes and terms and delivery and return and exchange and cancellation right arrangements, the stall or business site and time period, and orders and payment and vouchers and follow-up records. The output is sales results that can be completed and checked afterwards: a statement writing out the product and price and terms, an order completed and recorded face to face or same-spot delivery and payment collection, checkable payment and change and voucher and return and exchange and cancellation right statements, restocking and stall tidying records in some positions, and satisfaction follow-up and newcomer training that may be undertaken according to actual duties. The basis for judgment is the true information about the goods and the clearly marked price, consumer protection and cancellation and refund requirements, and local business and urban management and food safety (where food is involved) requirements and safety arrangements — not personal habit or job title.

Judgment one: Are the goods and quote truthful — do you describe the goods or services according to the true information and the clearly marked price and pricing unit, and state the total price and additional charges and delivery and return and exchange conditions, rather than quoting from impression or glossing over?

Judgment two: Are needs and demonstration checked — do you first check the customer's real needs and demonstrate face to face, then explain the price and terms, rather than continuing your pitch without regard to the customer or pushing hard?

Judgment three: Are the closing and order documented — are the order and price and delivery or same-spot delivery and payment collection accurately recorded with vouchers kept, rather than just taking the money without recording?

Judgment four: Are delivery and payment checkable — is delivery arranged as agreed or same-spot delivery and payment completed with change and voucher and invoice arrangements, rather than a verbal promise?

Judgment five: Are consumer rights and return and cancellation rights held — do you truthfully inform the customer of the cancellation right or return and refund conditions where applicable and handle accordingly, rather than avoiding it by closing on the spot?

The work of door-to-door sales workers and news and street vendors and related workers can be divided into three connected but independent work areas. The first is preparation and finding people: determine potential customers or a vending location, prepare samples and explanatory materials and payment money and change, set up the stall or ready the goods carried, and restock and tidy the display. The second is face-to-face selling and closing: explain the goods or services and prices and terms to potential customers and demonstrate, check customer needs and answer questions about product functions and benefits, persuade customers to buy, record or enter orders, and organize purchasing meetings and seek sponsorship when necessary. The third is delivery and payment and after-sales and mentoring: arrange delivery or same-spot delivery and payment with change and vouchers, distribute samples or materials, keep service records and contact customers to confirm satisfaction, and train newly recruited staff or other employees when necessary. All three work areas proceed within the true information about the goods and the clearly marked price, consumer protection and cancellation and refund requirements, and local business and urban management and food safety (where food is involved) requirements and safety arrangements.

Three things should govern the comparison: first, the work object (target customers and foot traffic locations and the goods carried, in-store customers and store staff, fixed routes and vehicles and cargo, organizational clients and placement budgets, organizational service needs and contracts, and on-site demonstration and promotional materials); second, the basis and authorization (the true information about the goods and the clearly marked price and consumer protection and local business requirements, retail and store rules, distribution and transport rules and driving requirements, advertising and service sales rules and contracts, and the applicability of each of the promotion and marketing rules); third, outputs and responsibility (who is responsible for face-to-face explanation and closing and payment collection and documentation, who is responsible for store staff and scheduling and performance, who is responsible for distribution and vehicles and cargo, who is responsible for organizational contracts and delivery, and who is responsible for on-site demonstration and leads). Where the three are inconsistent, the position's actual duties and the operator's and employer's authorization documents govern.

paragraphs: First-line supervisors of retail sales workers (41-1011.00)
Manage and coordinate retail sales staff in a store, responsible for scheduling and performance targets and supervision and service standards, and accountable for store sales operations.

Driver/sales workers (53-3031.00)

Retail salespersons (41-2031.00)

Scenarios and basis differ: retail salespersons serve in-store customers within a store and rely on store and retail rules; the occupation on this page proactively seeks customers at the customer's location or in the street, based on product information and clearly marked prices and consumer protection and local business and urban management requirements, and where applicable also involves the cancellation right and cooling-off period for off-premises transactions.

Advertising sales agents (41-3011.00)

Objects and outputs differ: advertising sales agents deal with media or advertising resources and organizational client placement plans and deliver under contract; the occupation on this page deals with physical goods or services and individual customers and delivers and collects payment per transaction, and does not bear media resource and placement plan and contract responsibility.

Sales representatives of services, except advertising, insurance, financial services, and travel (41-3091.00)

Objects and responsibility differ: sales representatives of services deal with organizational clients and service contracts and bear contract and delivery responsibility; the occupation on this page mainly deals with individual customers and single or face-to-face transactions, and does not bear organizational contract and professional service delivery responsibility.

If you want to sell services to organizations and manage contracts, you can choose the sales representative of services direction; if you want to focus on individual customers and same-spot closing, the occupation on this page is more suitable.
Demonstrators and product promoters (41-9011.00)

Outputs and basis differ: demonstrators and product promoters have on-site demonstration and sample distribution and lead collection as their main output, usually do not collect payment directly, and rely on promotion and marketing rules; the occupation on this page has persuading the customer to buy and completing the order and delivery and payment collection as its main output, based on product information and clearly marked prices and consumer protection requirements.

Cancellation runs until midnight of the third business day after the transaction, counting Sunday and federal holidays as excluded and Saturday as included, which is not the usual Monday-to-Friday working day; the seller must give oral notice at closing and a same-language voucher and two cancellation forms, and after a valid cancellation under 429.1 a refund within 10 business days, with state and local law checked separately. Articles 22 and 23 require the certificate and contract, leaving when the consumer refuses, and return disclosure and vouchers and the marked price; Article 24 requires remuneration based on the person's own direct sales income with a total of no more than 30% and at least monthly payment, and this applies only to that system and not to all sales industries; Article 25 allows return or exchange with the receipt within 30 days of purchase if unopened, handled within 7 days of the request, with other situations governed by law or contract. description.text: Door-to-Door Sales Workers, News and Street Vendors, and Related Workers (O*NET-SOC 41-9091.00) do face-to-face direct selling in communities and blocks and stalls and temporary sales sites: determine potential customers or a vending location and prepare samples and materials, explain the goods or services and price and demonstrate and check needs and handle objections, persuade customers to buy and record orders, arrange delivery or same-spot delivery and payment with vouchers, distribute samples or materials and restock and tidy the display, and keep records and follow up on satisfaction. United States scope: the BLS 2025 wage data median is 41,380 US dollars per year (19.89 US dollars per hour), with annual percentiles of 32,010／36,470／41,380／47,390／51,470 US dollars; employment was about 25,300 in 2024, the 2024—2034 projection is decline (-1% or lower), with about 2,700 projected openings; the preparation level is Job Zone 1-2 and the interest code is ECR; this wage scope is employed statistics, and OEWS does not cover the self-employed. Chinese mainland: business activity should involve truthful and comprehensive explanation, clearly marked prices, provision of vouchers, protection of personal information and handling of complaints, with business registration and urban management and food safety (where food is involved) carried out according to local rules; public statistics have not established an occupation-level wage scope, and this page visibly marks the gap in the relevant places.

subject.summary: Door-to-Door Sales Workers, News and Street Vendors, and Related Workers (United States side, O*NET-SOC 41-9091.00) is a non-store face-to-face direct selling position: selling goods or services door to door or along the street; determining potential customers or a vending location and preparing samples and explanatory materials and payment money, explaining the goods or services and price to potential customers and demonstrating, checking customer needs and answering questions about product functions and benefits, persuading customers to buy and recording or entering orders, and organizing purchasing meetings and seeking sponsorship when necessary; arranging delivery or same-spot delivery and payment with change and vouchers and invoices, distributing samples or materials, restocking and tidying the display, keeping service records and contacting customers to confirm satisfaction, and training newly recruited staff or other employees when necessary; the employment form may be employed, commission-based or self-employed (individual business operator). United States scope: the BLS 2025 wage data median is 41,380 US dollars per year (19.89 US dollars per hour), with annual percentiles of 32,010／36,470／41,380／47,390／51,470 US dollars (hourly percentiles 15.39／17.54／19.89／22.78／24.74); this scope is employed wage statistics, OEWS does not cover the self-employed, and commissions and expense reimbursement and irregular business income do not necessarily enter the same scope; the O*NET summary page gives employment of about 25,300 in 2024, a 2024—2034 projection of decline (-1% or lower) and about 2,700 projected job openings (the source gives only the category and not a specific percentage, and this page states it in the original wording); the preparation level is Job Zone 1-2 (SVP below 6.0), the interest code is ECR, the education feedback is 57% less than high school and 43% high school or equivalent, and there are 14 tasks; the work context includes continuous contact with others 52% (another 43% in contact most of the time), face-to-face discussions every day 36% (another 50% weekly or more), telephone conversations every day 55%, dealing with external customers or the public extremely important 70%, decision freedom very much 88%, precision or accuracy extremely important 17%, facing time pressure every day 17%, working hours irregular 67%, standing about half the time 46%, dealing with unpleasant or angry or rude people monthly or more 38%, conflict situations yearly or more 50%, level of competition extremely competitive 13%, and use email every day 70%. Chinese mainland scope: business activity should involve truthful and comprehensive explanation, clearly marked prices, provision of vouchers, protection of personal information and handling of complaints (under the Consumer Rights and Interests Protection Law of the People's Republic of China); engaging in individual business and vending and mobile business should meet local market supervision and urban management requirements, and where food is involved should also meet food safety requirements (cited by regulation and rule name and general requirements, without checking article numbers item by item); on the United States side, in door-to-door or other off-premises transactions covered by the federal rule, the seller must disclose the three-business-day cancellation right to the consumer under 16 CFR Part 429 (the FTC cooling-off rule), and whether it applies depends on amount, location, goods or services and exceptions. This occupation has no uniform access-type professional qualification in the Chinese mainland. Public statistics have not established an occupation-level wage scope corresponding to this occupation, and this page truthfully retains the gap.
